title: Why did this part break so quickly on my 2023 pickup?
author: John Paul
bullets: A 2023 Ford Maverick's front sway bar links broke at 22,000 miles, suggesting potential quality issues.
Torx-Plus fasteners provide stronger, more precise fits for automated assembly, reducing strip risks.
AAA's Car Doctor suggests CTEK and Deltran's Battery Tender products for maintaining rarely used vehicle batteries.

title: 4 injured in Boston school bus rollover, police say
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Four adults injured in a school bus rollover in Mattapan, Boston, on Thursday; no children were on the bus.
The accident occurred around 1:10 p.m. near 1000 Harvard St., and the victims were taken to a nearby hospital.
The bus was found on its side, and the cause of the rollover is currently unknown, police report.

title: Drake Maye struggled during two-minute drill, and other takeaways from Day 11 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Drake Maye threw two interceptions during a two-minute drill, drawing successful plays from Marcus Jones and Kevin Byard.
Marcus Bryant took first-team reps at left tackle with Will Campbell limited; Caleb Lomu remained with the second team.
Rookie linebacker Gabe Jacas received first-team practice reps as he progresses in his return to play plan.

title: A beloved Cape Cod restaurant is closing after 21 years
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Chach Restaurant in Provincetown is closing on November 2 after 21 years in operation.
Owners Viola Briseño and Sharon Bowes cite the demanding nature of the restaurant business as a reason for the closure.
Chach, known for scratch-made dishes like Eggs Benedict, has received an outpouring of support from the community.

title: Navy says it can’t help recover wreckage of Gloucester fishing boat Lily Jean
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: The US Navy declined to assist in recovering the wreckage of the Lily Jean fishing vessel off Cape Ann.
Gov. Maura Healey had requested Navy help to recover possible evidence from the boat's hard drive and video recorder.
The US Coast Guard and NTSB are leading the investigation, and it's unclear if the cause of sinking is known.

title: Councilor Flynn blocks measure calling for response to elimination of protected status for Haitians
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Boston Councilor Ed Flynn blocked a resolution for city action on the loss of Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Syrians.
The resolution, introduced by Councilor Ruthzee Louijeune, aimed to coordinate resources for displaced Boston residents.
Flynn's objection sends the resolution to the Committee on Housing and Community Development, delaying an official vote.

title: The Cape Wildlife Center needed 31,725 frozen mice. The public stepped up.
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Cape Wildlife Center in Barnstable needed 31,725 frozen mice annually for animals after losing a longtime free supplier.
Public donations quickly met the center's goal, avoiding an additional $30,000-$45,000 annual cost for buying mice.
The center expressed gratitude for the community's support, ensuring uninterrupted care for its wildlife patients.

title: The Red Sox just did something the team hasn’t accomplished since 1912
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: The Red Sox have won nine consecutive series, last achieved in 1912.
Boston's streak includes wins against the Dodgers and all American League East opponents.
The team is currently 30-5 since late June, entering the playoff race after a poor start.

title: Boston will be overflowing with Hobbits this weekend. Breakfast is involved.
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Dominic Monaghan and 'Hobbit' castmates celebrate the 25th anniversary of 'Lord of the Rings' at Fan Expo Boston.
Fans can attend 'An Evening with the Hobbits' and 'Second Breakfast' events at the convention center August 7-9.
Upcoming project 'The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum' directed by Andy Serkis slated for release December 2027.

title: These are the Mass. beaches closed for swimming as next potential heat wave moves in
author: Peter Chianca and Heather Alterisio
bullets: Approximately 50 Massachusetts beaches were closed on Thursday due to water quality concerns.
Beach closures result from factors like bacterial exceedance and harmful cyanobacteria blooms.
The interactive state dashboard updates hourly to reflect current water quality conditions across beaches.
